Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear asks and the PDF. Short answers up front, detail below:

- Yes: in a Private (VPC) deployment with customer-controlled storage, data stored in the tenant storage layer is confined to the provisioned region (Frankfurt) and is not replicated to other regions unless explicitly configured during onboarding.
- Evidence: we can provide (a) time-stamped deletion proofs (operation IDs and tombstone manifests), (b) per-tenant access logs exported to your audit bucket, and (c) network flow summaries showing no egress to non-EU IP ranges.

Details / next steps:
1) Residency guarantee: Redwood’s Private control plane is configurable to bind storage endpoints to a customer-managed S3 bucket or an on-prem NFS. When bound to your Frankfurt bucket (recommended), the runtime treats the bucket as the authoritative object store; snapshots and persistent state remain in-region. We will add an explicit residency clause into the onboarding SOW for your account.

2) Proof-of-delete and attestation options: we support three levels of attestations — self-service API deletion logs (for operational use), signed attestations (PDF) from Redwood with operation IDs and retention timeline, and third-party audit packages (SOC2 + configurable snapshot of deletion artifacts). The signed attestation includes a hash of the deleted manifest and timestamp.

3) Logs & chain-of-custody: we can configure per-tenant audit export to your SIEM (S3 or syslog endpoint) and provide sequential operation logs (append-only) for the life of the tenant. Those logs include actor, operation ID, object keys, and source IP.

4) Architecture diagram and sample evidence: attaching the VPC diagram and an audit template for your compliance team to review.

If agreeable, I’ll loop in our compliance lead and Karthik from sales to align the SOW language and any credit for evidence collection.

Available for a short call Thursday afternoon (CEST) if you want to walk through the artifacts.

Hi Sophie — looping in a couple of contractual points you may find useful for the compliance review: 

- SOW clause: we typically include a regional residency commitment tied to the tenant's provisioning region and a migration exception that requires written approval for any cross-region replication.
- Retention/deletion SLA: standard is a 30-day soft-delete window followed by tombstone removal; for audits we can shorten this and provide immediate hard-delete workflows as part of the enterprise onboarding.
- Evidence delivery: we can provide an export package (signed manifest + logs + network flow sample) on request; for regulated customers we offer an annual attestation addendum.

If you have any specific phrasing your legal/regulatory team requires, share that and we’ll map it to the SOW.

Sophie — answering each point and attaching a sample signed attestation PDF draft for review.

1) Signed attestation: yes — our standard attestation includes a SHA-256 hash of the deleted manifest, issuance timestamp, Redwood operation ID, and signer metadata (name, role, signing key id). We can optionally include an HMAC field keyed to a customer-provided secret for extra verification.

2) Access log retention: default retention is 90 days in the control plane. For customers with audit needs we offer configurable retention up to 36 months; for 24 months we will add that to the onboarding SOW and configure the audit export to your S3 bucket with lifecycle rules.

3) Network flow summary: we provide aggregated flow summaries by default (allowed/denied, regional egress counts). For audits we can provide detailed flow logs (source IP, dest IP, port, timestamp) as a time-bounded export. Those exports can be delivered to your SIEM endpoint or via secure transfer.

Operational proof-of-delete sequence we will provide once the deletion is performed:
- Operation request ID (UUID)
- Pre-delete snapshot manifest hash
- Soft-delete tombstone manifest (if enabled)
- Hard-delete confirmation with post-delete manifest hash (if requested)
- Signed attestation PDF containing the hashes and operation IDs

Next steps: I’ve attached the sample signed attestation PDF and a checklist we’ll use for the compliance package. Proposed call: Thursday 2025-07-17 at 14:00 CEST to walk through artifacts and SOW language.

Thanks — looping in Marissa from Solutions Ops to coordinate the evidence export window.
